title: Defense's prohibition on foreign commercial dependencies is a structural demand driver, not a preference
content:
The note records that the "Defense industry has a hard requirement to avoid dependencies on foreign commercial players", appearing under manufacturing rather than as a separate sector.

The significance is the word *hard*. Most buying arguments require persuading someone that a property is valuable; this one is imposed from outside the buying decision and cannot be traded away by a procurement officer who likes a competing product. It converts self-hostability and open licensing from differentiators into eligibility criteria.

That is the same mechanism found in the tool screen, where a licence that forbids production use without payment excludes a vendor from sovereignty-constrained buyers regardless of technical merit. Where the constraint binds, it decides the shortlist before features are compared.
description: Recorded as a hard requirement to avoid dependencies on foreign commercial players — an externally imposed constraint that favours self-hostable open-source infrastructure.
